newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee officials discuss soluble problems.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee officials discuss soluble problems.

text.p: A working group of Brazilian coffee officials met today to discuss problems facing the country's soluble coffee industry but no decisions on measures were reached, said a roasting industry official.

"The soluble coffee industry is facing difficulties becuse prices of robusta coffee in the international market are lower than the coffee the industry buys in Brazil," said Americo Sato, vice-president of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association.
"We are therefore looking at ways to ensure the industry does not loss its competivity because of this," he said.
Options could include importing coffee but this did not have the support for the time being of all factions within the sector, Sato said.

The government for the last time last month included in its monthly auctions coffee purely for the soluble industry. In a second such sale on March 5, some 82,610 60-bags of a total 256,990 bags will be exclusively for the soluble industry.
The industry will also be able to participate in bidding for the remaining 174,380 bags.

At the meeting today were representatives from the roasting and soluble industries, exporter and producer groups as well as officials from the Industry and Commerce Ministry, including Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department.
Another meeting of the group was likely to take place around March 10, Sato said.

However no decisions were likely until the next meeting of Brazil's new joint private and public sector coffee council which is scheduled to meet on April 28 in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais state, he added.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
